liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer finds this performance textbook perfect, and also singles out a superb Jack Straw opening the show [20]
- **Drums** (1 other source): Drums segues into Nobody's Fault But Mine, followed by Not Fade Away, per the uploader's setlist [1]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the finest Stella Blue version they have ever heard [19]
- **U.S. Blues** (1 other source): U.S. Blues is listed as the encore in this audience recording's notes [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-05-08.136537.aud.wise.minches.flac24** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 163 min [1]
- **gd81-05-08.sbd.miller.28300.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 162 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer is glad a good-quality soundboard source exists, credited to Charlie Miller [20]
- **gd1981-05-08.mtx.seamons.92002.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 166 min; rated 4.27/5 by 15 [7]. Said about its sound: Matrix sounds smooth and full, with excellent balance between the soundboard and audience sources; Audience recordings add life to an otherwise flat soundboard; most 1981 soundboards would benefit from the same blending [23][24]
- **gd1981-05-08.sbd.miller.95764.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 162 min; rated 3.38/5 by 8 [8]
- **gd1981-05-08.175118.sbd.miller.phase-repair.flac1644**: soundboard; 19 songs; 161 min [9]

## Around the show

- Ken Kesey joins the Rhythm Devils on harmonica [19]
- Ken Kesey plays harmonica on part of the show; the second set is called incredible [7]
- Ken Kesey plays harmonica during Drums and U.S. Blues [8]
- Ken Kesey plays harmonica during Drums and U.S. Blues [9]
- Reviewer says most other 1981 soundboards could use the same audience-source boost as this matrix [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-05-08.136537.aud.wise.minches.flac24**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by David Minches; source: Cassette Audience Master: Recorded By Jeff Hellman (lead deck) > Eddie Claridge (2nd deck) > Jim Wise (3rd deck); Sennheiser MD421 Dynamic Cardioid… [1]
- **gd81-05-08.sbd.miller.28300.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [6]
- **gd1981-05-08.mtx.seamons.92002.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Barry Glassberg and Jim Wise; transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: MATRIX MIX: SBD/2 AUD (About 60%/40%) [7]. Also: Matrix is roughly 60% soundboard and 40% audience, patched and transferred by Charlie Miller; Audience source: Barry Glassberg taped with Nakamichi 700s to Sony TC-D5M cassette; Mark Cohen transferred to DAT via Tascam decks [7]
- **gd1981-05-08.sbd.miller.95764.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Dat (44.1k) [8]. Also: Soundboard remaster uses a Nakamichi 700 audience source to patch Playing In The Band and Sugar Magnolia; channels swapped, patches fixed [8]
- **gd1981-05-08.175118.sbd.miller.phase-repair.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 14, 2025; source: SBD > Cassette Master > DAT (44.1k) [9]. Also: This release repairs a vocal phase problem in an earlier Miller soundboard and adds two patches to Playing In The Band [9]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by John Rottet Grateful Dead: [1981-05-08 Nassau Coliseum, Uniondale, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1981-05-08-nassau-coliseum-uniondale-ny-usa/) [32]
